words: Craig argues cited critical scholars never disputed his majority claim in prior debates, so naming them does not establish historical disagreement over the three core facts.
critique: Strongest feature: Craig directly answers the dispute over majority New Testament scholarship with his Barr quotation and reports that debated critics Crossan, Lüdemann, and Borg never challenged majority acceptance of all three core facts. Principal limitation: The excerpt supplies neither quoted wording nor any survey, sample, or account of what each scholar accepts, so silence in debates weakly warrants a precise majority claim and scarcely resolves later alternatives. Live burden: Craig must substantiate scholarly consensus, distinguish acceptance of every fact from acceptance of his resurrection inference, and answer the nondecisively contacted challenge from late alternative accounts. Locked score: The exact score of 72 fits because direct engagement makes responsiveness and relevance stronger, while unsupported scholarly counting leaves evidence warrant and calibration materially weaker.
